label: verify-q2-theory-lean

claims.claim: Attenuation: with cov(y,e)=0 and cov(p,e)=0, r(p,y+e)^2 <= var y/(var y+var e) and |r| <= sqrt of that; tight via attenuation_tight.
claims.source_says: theorem pearson_attenuation ... (hye : cov P y e = 0) (hpe : cov P p e = 0) ... (pearson P p (y+e))^2 ≤ var P y / (var P y + var P e) ∧ |pearson ...| ≤ Real.sqrt (...)
claims.note: Statement matches; also needs var p>0 and var y+var e>0, and attenuation_tight shows r^2 equals the bound with the truth as predictor.

claims.claim: Total variance on pooled data: var y = between + within; target-only predictor has r^2 = between/total and cannot reduce MSE below within.
claims.source_says: theorem total_variance (hm : IsGroupMean P g y m) : var P y = between + within; r2_target_only: cov^2/(var*var y) = between/var y; target_only_floor: within ≤ MSE of any f∘g.
claims.note: All three theorems match the plain words, with positivity side conditions for the r^2 one.

claims.claim: Cycle closure: path-additive predictor sums to zero around closed walks; with additive truth errors also sum to zero; pairwise-uncorrelated cycle errors impossible unless zero; exchangeable errors have correlation -1/(n-1).
claims.source_says: exchangeable_cycle_deviations concludes only: s + ((n : ℝ) - 1) * c = 0 (docstring: 'i.e. error correlation -1/(n-1)'). deviations_not_independent: E[ε_i ε_i] = 0 for all i.
claims.note: Cycle and zero-second-moment theorems match, but -1/(n-1) correlation is only implied informally (c/s with s>0), not stated as a theorem.

claims.claim: Kernel check passed: errors=0, sorryAx=0, 16/16 axiom lines, axioms only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
claims.source_says: Q2Theory.lean errors=0 sorryAx=0 axiom-lines=16/16 ... ALL CHECKED: no errors, no sorryAx
claims.note: Log reproduces errors, sorryAx and 16/16; the axiom names are not in the log and I did not inspect them, but the file has zero 'sorry' and sha256 matches.

overall: Three of four claims hold. The cycle claim is partly supported, because the -1/(n-1) correlation appears only in a docstring while the theorem proves s+(n-1)c=0. The kernel-check claim is also partly supported, because the log shows errors=0, sorryAx=0 and 16/16 but does not list the axiom names. I did not re-run Lean.
